title: Panel example: Data and known coefficients
summary: Firm quality is deliberately visible to the simulation author and omitted from the fitted models. Experience depends on that quality. Errors share shocks within firms, while different firms remain independent. The known coefficients describe the constructed process; one fitted sample will not reproduce them exactly.

title: Panel example: Pooled, fixed-effects and random-effects fits
summary: The three models use the same regressors and year indicators. Unit FE remove the additive firm effect from the linear equation. Firm-clustered covariance addresses dependence under the constructed independent-firm sampling structure; it does not remove omitted variables.

title: Panel example: Within-between decomposition
summary: Each regressor is split into its firm mean and its deviation from that mean. The RE fit includes both parts for all regressors, so between coefficients can be estimated. The within slopes agree with FE in this balanced linear specification. An unrestricted unit-FE fit would instead absorb the firm means.

title: Panel example: A joint slope restriction
summary: In the mean/deviation parameterization, the usual RE slope restriction equates the within and between coefficients. The joint Wald test uses the fitted clustered covariance. Its result concerns these restrictions within this linear model; it cannot certify exogeneity.

title: Panel example: GEE and working covariance
summary: The exchangeable working correlation differs from the simulated AR(1) errors. Sandwich covariance can be useful despite working-correlation misspecification under suitable mean and exogeneity conditions. This pooled GEE mean still omits correlated firm quality.

title: Panel example: A working variance model
summary: The random-intercept model attributes covariance to a firm component and an idiosyncratic component under its working model. The simulated serial correlation is richer than that specification. Its ICC is therefore a model-dependent summary, not a causal percentage of performance attributable to firms.

title: Panel example: A separate dynamic panel
summary: This section temporarily replaces the data with a dynamic process whose lag coefficient is .5. Native Arellano-Bond estimation uses lagged outcome instruments under explicit serial-correlation and timing restrictions. The original static panel is restored afterward.

title: Panel example: Reporting the fitted comparisons
summary: The table and confidence interval come from actual fitted estimates. Report the sample, model, covariance, units and interpretation. The dynamic model uses a different sample and is not placed in the static comparison table.
